title: Temptation and character
summary: When desire, appetite, or ego pull you off course — return to Jesus, not a self-fix ladder.
graceGuardrail: Naming temptation is not earning holiness. Character grows as fruit of grace, not as the price of being loved.
framing: You do not come here to score yourself. You come here to tell the truth, receive mercy, and take one faithful step.
why: Everyone faces pull. Scripture names it so you can walk honestly with God — not so you can shame yourself into looking holy.

sections.heading: What this life area is for
paragraphs: Temptation is the pull toward what God calls unwise or unloving. Character is who you are becoming as you walk with Jesus.
This shelf is for people who feel that pull — pride, greed, envy, anger, appetite, lust — and want Scripture that leads back to grace.

sections.heading: How to walk this shelf
paragraphs: Keep the centre clear: Jesus already came for sinners. Repentance is turning toward Him, not punishing yourself first.
bullets: Be honest — name the pull without dressing it up
Receive mercy — God meets you in truth, not in performance
Take one step — a prayer, a boundary, a faithful habit, or a trusted conversation
Read next — return to Jesus and the Gospel whenever shame gets loud

sections.heading: Paths to grow here
paragraphs: Some paths already have a Compass page. Others will land on this shelf over time. Always keep the Gospel under your feet.

sections.heading: One truth to hold
paragraphs: Temptation is common. Escape and help are real. You are not the only one — and you are not beyond mercy. (1 Corinthians 10:13; Hebrews 4:15–16)

sixtySecond: Name one pull you feel today in one honest sentence before God.
Say out loud: “Grace first. I turn toward Jesus, not toward self-punishment.”
Choose one small faithful step — a prayer, a pause, or asking a trusted person to walk with you.
prayer: Father, You see the pulls on my heart. Thank You that Jesus meets me with mercy. Form my character by Your Spirit, and keep me from treating holiness like a ladder. Amen.

scripture.insight: Temptation is real and common — and God provides a way to endure.
Jesus sympathises with weakness. Draw near for mercy and help.
Character fruit grows from the Spirit, not from grinding harder alone.
